extracted.intended_audience: prospective grant applicants and partners (nonprofits, research institutions, and private companies), and internal program teams working on Gates Foundation grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation selects, funds, manages, monitors, and closes grants and strategic investments, including expectations for applicants and partners. Covers the four-stage grantmaking process, funding vehicles, evaluation, cost policies, and global access requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to create measurable impact on foundation priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees and projects are chosen according to their ability to create impact on the foundation’s priority issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams have deep expertise in science, data, and policy and select grantees/projects that can create impact on priority issues; focus on developing long-term strategies for critical domestic US and global issues where the foundation can have the greatest catalytic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with team strategic priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must align with the specific strategic priorities of the relevant topic-focused team at the foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program officers seek out projects that align with the team’s strategic priorities—often in consultation with other foundation colleagues, researchers, policymakers, and organizations working in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening to local context and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Start by listening to the people who experience the challenges and consult local advocates and community leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask what people need that isn’t available, what barriers stand in their way, and what geographic or cultural factors are unique; this local input informs project design and fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for transformative, scalable solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus most investment on solutions that could have transformative impact and can reach scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek projects that can be catalytic; avoid substituting for public- or private-sector spending; consider where foundation resources and relationships can make the greatest difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time‑bound investments and plan for scale-up by others
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside core global health institutions, investments are time-bound with others expected to step in for scale-up and delivery over the long term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design investments with a clear timeframe and transition/scale plans so that long-term delivery is carried on by appropriate public/private actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-stage grantmaking process adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: All teams follow the same four-stage grantmaking process: (1) developing the project, (2) soliciting proposals, (3) proposal review and approval, (4) grant allocation and project closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration of each phase depends on project complexity and partner capacity/geography; applicants should expect these sequential stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 1: Project development by program officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers identify and develop project concepts aligned with team priorities, often in consultation with experts and field organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program officers may proactively seek projects or refine concepts with input from colleagues, researchers, policymakers, and practitioners in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 2: Soliciting proposals (direct, discussion, RFP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams may solicit proposals by direct solicitation, discussion/invitation, or issuing public/private RFPs depending on scope and desire to broaden grantee search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public RFPs (including Grand Challenges) are posted on the website; private RFPs are directed to specific organizations. Prospective grantees are given guidelines and templates for proposals and budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide guidance and templates for proposals and budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation gives each prospective grantee guidelines and templates for developing a proposal and a budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided templates and follow instructions to ensure proposals align with team expectations and facilitate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 3: Multi-level proposal review and due diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted materials are reviewed by program officers with internal (and sometimes external) experts; teams perform due diligence on organizational, legal, financial, and risk aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due diligence includes confirming tax-exempt status (where relevant), determining partnership structure, assessing risk, and involving legal and financial teams as needed. Complex grants undergo more levels of review; a foundation executive makes the final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm organizational and partnership eligibility and risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess applicant organization’s tax-exempt status, capacity, how partnership should be structured, and overall risk profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assessment may involve legal and financial teams and affects approval and contract structuring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreements must specify results, measurement, schedule, and payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Before funded activities begin, the foundation and grantee sign an agreement that includes intended results and targets, measurement and reporting milestones, delivery schedule, and payment schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts formalize expectations and milestones; these terms guide monitoring and payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 4: Active grant management and closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the grant life, program officers and grantees stay in close touch to monitor progress, address challenges, and document results at closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open communication is crucial; program officers may join advisory committees or boards; grantees produce a final report summarizing results and lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing collaboration, monitoring, and adaptive management
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation works closely with partners to formulate plans, monitor progress, make strategic adjustments, and ensure products/services are accessible and affordable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaboration during the funding term includes joint planning, progress monitoring, and course corrections as needed to achieve impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and evaluation focused on critical metrics and high‑quality evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: From the earliest phases, define desired results, data needed to measure progress/results, and how to evaluate that data; focus reporting on critical metrics rather than all activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nature and frequency of measurement depend on work type; the foundation ensures grantees have capacity/support to generate and analyze high-quality evidence; avoids one-size-fits-all prescriptions (see Evaluation Policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require open sharing of scientific data and results
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of scientific research, the foundation requires that resulting data and results be shared openly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-data expectations apply to scientific projects; see foundation policies for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial efficiency while covering grantee costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for financial efficiency and effectiveness while ensuring that the grantee’s costs for delivering results are fully covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with prospective grantees to gain a complete and accurate understanding of project costs; compare grant compositions item-by-item when comparing to other funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible treatment of indirect costs for research institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations may count indirect 'facilities and administrative' costs as direct costs for grants to universities and research institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project management, lab fees, IT and data charges may be allowable as direct costs in Gates Foundation grants; see the Indirect Cost Policy for details and item-by-item comparisons to government grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of funding vehicle: committed grants vs strategic investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide committed grants to organizations for measurable impact (over 90% of charitable giving) and strategic investments to for-profit companies via the Strategic Investment Fund when private-sector expertise is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committed grants fund nonprofit and public-sector partners; SIF designs partnerships with private companies that can include equity, loans, or volume guarantees to further philanthropic goals (not to generate income).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global access and affordability requirements for investments and funded products
rubrics_metrics.description: Investments and funding are bound by global access requirements that mandate prompt and broad dissemination of scientific knowledge and that products developed with funding be broadly available and affordable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global Access Statement provides further details; any financial returns from strategic investments are reinvested in programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Strategic Investment Fund (SIF) for private-sector partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: When teams want private-sector science and technology expertise, work via the SIF which has a separate budget for funding companies’ work on charitable projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIF designs instruments (equity, loans, guarantees) in collaboration with program teams to achieve philanthropic goals while upholding global access requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for coalitions and multi-stakeholder collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Support and help fund coalitions of governments, donors, researchers, communities, and companies so all parties can collaborate on solving urgent problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes complex, deeply rooted issues that require multi-party collaboration and sustained effort beyond the foundation’s own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics reporting mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation offers options for reporting issues that raise ethical concerns, including anonymous/confidential reporting via EthicsPoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees, grantees, vendors, and partners can use these channels to report ethical concerns related to foundation-funded work.
